b: about the emerald lies upon the windowsill, drinking the shimmer of midday’s last light as an ocean sips of river. the sunbeam sifts by refraction into its gloaming wells, thinning and winnowing as it travels a distance that only light can. cold and pale it falls over the face of the girl at its heart, suspended within the verdant bloom of a million rays mingled. to the stranger’s eye, she is pinioned eternal by the facets of the emerald world. all range of motion is demarcated by still, artificial lines. her wings broaden only two-thirds of their length before pressing full against cold, angular contour. but to her, there is only slenderest distinction between the stone part of the world and the shadow that tends to it. [[more]] ■ she studies the banners of light that stream through her prism form or fall nearby. she studies dust in descent. she is placed in boxes where she reflects on darkness, and dropped in pouches where she reflects on motion. each time she catches glimpse of another gem, she closes her eyes and tries to engrave the image on the back of her eyelids. she wonders if they make an effort to remember her too. for abrupt, fleeting slivers of time, she is lifted. encompassed within majestic hands that touch and turn her. these too she forcibly sears into her memory, as stimulation to reflect upon over and over until drained to blur. she learns to differentiate their fingerprints by tactility. at times, they are wreathed in cloth as she is cradled in stone. this makes it more difficult to interpret what is happening to her outside face, but does not at least blemish with trace oils. for longer, langourous moments — luxuriate, ephemeral, as though blinking amidst a dream — she is worn. shining at the crest of a golden crown. bright upon a warm delicate neckline. this is something she prizes. brighter than the reflections she sees in other gems, more of a freefall than falling itself. to be adored. glorified. ■ in the clearing of her heart sits the understanding that she is a maiden — one who exists to maintain the world. to care for and to edify. yet she cannot herself wash away the dust that at times sprinkles the gem’s surface, nor polish its lustre, nor seal it in everlasting sanctuary. just as soon could the universe turn itself inside out as she could trace her lips over the lines of her glimmering outside face. the tools that avail themselves to hand: her minute form, her encapsulated voice, and the light in which she is cast. she turns inward. she defines symbols with which to interpret the world (stone, shadow, adoration) and ways to express those symbols. when those outside speak, it reaches her only as a dull warm murmur - she emulates the sound. with this, she turns herself wholly upon the task of glorification. serving the gem with her love. adoring it as she was adored. she fills her mind with poems that flourish into hymns that flower into soliloquies. she fills the chamber of the emerald world with her voice. she impresses her worship into the interior facets that cradle her with delicate, reverent kisses. she sings gently to the outside facets, adamant against dust and smears and all else that defiles. she sings of the loveliness of the shadow, ever-resolute to exalt and reify. ■ she finds herself flecked with blood again. this happens every other often: she is violently stolen away, only to be fiercely guarded as before, but now in new hands. she reflects upon herself as an object of desire. she is the most valuable thing that she has ever known and ever will. a thing that commands need, that defines and forms the cusp of ambition itself. that others find their very lives to be dross before the face of. a symbol of power — which as symbols do, gives the world meaning. this, she thinks, is wonderful. when her possessors gaze into her gleaming depths, she whispers sweet allurance. faint, as though an echo passed through long caverns. only in total stillness might it be heard, softer than a single trembling leaf. “this is your reward for owning me,” she sings. “look upon the fullness of my beauty,” she sings, “and see the breadth of my adoration for you. all that i am exists as a testament to your glory. own me forever!” she turns her love honed over ages upon her owners. they bend like flowers underfoot. every word of it is sincere, for each time she has true faith in they who vanquished the last. individual hands blur together, and she speaks to them as manifestations of their role itself, with whom she shares a long history. the other. the conqueror. the counterpart. her words are heeded. yet even so they seem fated to fumble and die, much to her chagrin. once she is even, astoundingly, misplaced. until finally, she finds herself in the hands of a grand and magnificent witch. her stately hands run cold with sweat. they tremble like a schoolgirl’s. she is pierced by the jewel’s beauty in a way that no blade has ever known. “i’ll take you away,” she whispers. “into the formless dark. where you won’t have the slenderest hope of escape, nor i. not by loss. not by decay. you will know no hand but mine!” “then i will love you there,” says the jewel. “until it is formless light.”

b: empty-heart-princess : little sprite’s storybook once upon a time, a strange and sharp-toothed lady sat in the boughs of an oak tree, quite alone and quite out of place in the middle of the fen. it gnarled and twisted towards the sky, along the ground; an ancient yearning pushing it in every which direction! the lady had nestled herself in a crook of the tree and begun to read; she recited poetry in dulcet tones, of love and grief and hateful violence, and the wicked dross between all three. the little sprite could not help but flit down from his home among the leaves and listen. she read poem after poem after poem, and each word captivated him; and in between she would pause and take notes, and he would grow frightfully bored until she began again. with each break he grew more frustrated. playing with the ladybugs and aphids did less and less to soothe his irritation. after an especially long poem, to his outrage, the lady took whole minutes to herself! he barrelled down to confront this injustice: “humans! joyless! dreadful! who must each thing by pen and wit command in full, so ne'er they lend a word its own exhort!” his voice rang like the crisp of autumn air. he reddened his face and crossed his arms and puffed his cheeks in the most vicious pout he could muster. “hmph!” the lady jumped, and sought the source of the insult, until she settled on the little sprite and her eyes softened in delight. barely more than an inch high, held aloft on beeswings and cuddled up in a coat so furry as to threaten to swallow him. iridescent hair scattered past his shoulders. “oh my! what a darling little fairy. why, you are the prettiest thing i have ever beheld. your coat, too–who made that for you?” his pout faltered in the face of the compliment. “the coat was made by my own hand, of cast-off wings, the orphans of the secret things a moth becomes, when their time as moth is up; a stitcher’s pride in it i place.” “as is well-deserved! such fine craftsmanship must surely have taken ages to perfect. how old are you, little thing?” he creased his brow and clenched his fists and tried and failed to hold onto his indignity. “born i was a week ago, now wise and agéd i’ve become; still do i recall the times when leaves were red, not gold.” the lady laughs lightly. “to think i should meet such an elder! and yet so youthful and spry. tell me, what should i call you?” “a name one keeps a secret thing–this i know by wisdom of my many days. you, i think, may call me sprite.” “sprite! how lovely. you were fond of my reading, weren’t you? i would love to continue, but the sun is setting and soon it’ll be dark. i promise, little sprite, i’ll read to you tomorrow.” and she closed her book and hefted her walking-stick, then turned back and asked: “do you fear the dark, sprite?” “never! darkness but a trifle is; always comes, in time, the dawn.” “wise indeed!” and so she leaves. and the next afternoon the lady did return to that oak in that fen, and sit herself in the crook of its boughs, and read again. she read plays, of assassins and their daggers and their knives. and all the while the little sprite straddled her wrist and listened and only mildly grumbled when she paused. soon again, the sun was setting; “dear sprite, i’m afraid i must go now.” and she closed her book, and hefted her walking-stick, then turned back and asked: “do you fear knives, sprite?” “hah! a knife is naught except a toy, for to carve and cut the cloth. one must its teeth regard, but fear? never!” “careful indeed!” and so she leaves. once more, on the third afternoon, the lady came again to the little sprite’s home, and settled herself in the crook of its boughs, and read to him. he settled on her shoulder, leaned against her neck, and listened to stories of terrible isolation and grief. he didn’t even complain when she took her time between passages. but again the sun sunk low in the sky. “precious sprite, i must take my leave.” and she closed her book, and hefted her walking-stick, then turned back and asked: “do you fear being alone, sprite?” “alone? all my life before have i in isolation lived; how could i fear the one and only thing i’ve known?” “steadfast indeed!” and so she leaves. but the fourth afternoon, as the lady arrives to the tree again and places herself in the crook of its boughs, she asks a question. “little sprite, so long have i known you, all these many days; more than half a week has come and gone since our first meeting. and yet i still do not know your name. surely, you could entrust such a steadfast friend with your secret?” he considers. he hems. he haws. he should not–but indeed, so long has he known her, and in that time he hasn’t seen one ounce of ill-will or malice from her. surely, he could entrust such a steadfast friend with his secret. “to you, my friend, an indiscretion i might make; for ne'er in all our time together have you wanted for the power over me it may provide. you alone may call me: bran.” “bran? i see. what a lovely name. come along, now, there are things i must show you.” “my friend, adore you as i do, i must not from my home go far; your tales must to me suffice.” “bran, poor thing, i did not ask. come along.” and so he did, all the way home; and i taught him all the fears to which he had been so naïve. i taught him darknesses that do not break for any dawn, lightless months on lightless months until he forgets all sight. i taught him blades which cut so much more than cloth–toys, true, but only to me, until his wings are so torn through as to be useless. i taught him isolation so much crueler than what he thought he knew, no bees or birds to keep him company, until he forgot the world might ever contain someone besides himself. and then my work began, secret things of which i will not speak, not even to you, my dear, steadfast friend. and when the work was done, i beheld my opus with a stitcher’s pride, hard won over decades of practice and failure: you, my sweet little genevieve. who fears the dark. who fears the knives. who fears being alone. but i will shelter you from all these things, and you will be by my side forever.

x: i ended up watching season 2 of omega slut alexis . on the surface, it’s not a complex work. for the first fifteen minutes of an episode,…
b: i ended up watching season 2 of omega slut alexis . on the surface, it’s not a complex work. for the first fifteen minutes of an episode, bad stuff happens. alexis loses her mailbox on a busy street. alexis’ bathwater turns to poisonous tree frogs. alexis is abducted by goth mermaids into an alcove of the school’s bottomless swimming pool. alexis can instantly dissolve any problem. each element of the world is ultimately biddable, so long as she sincerely tries to understand and care for it. and she does. every event and thing touches or moves her somehow. her most composed and distant is only two steps from weeping with the pathos of empathy as vast as space. if it looks like something actually horrid and unrecoverable is going to happen, a closet nearby slams opens and she emerges, eyes blazing and tearstreaked. and then she stops it: lovingly, kindly, in a way which makes everyone involved better off. [[more]] stubborn. recalcitrant. rather than being good, reality utterly inundates her in problems. tricky ones. where she’s not sure she wants to break a problem. or she’s not sure if she’s looking at a problem. or she’s unsure what she’s looking at, generally. or she’s forgotten what it means for something to be a problem. ■ (she wears the mannerisms of an adult, while others have the lilt and overaction of children. this much is strange, because every other character is her parent in some way, new ones introduced with every episode. each can credibly claim to be her creator: one is her mother. one is her grandmother. one built her heart. one designed her personality to specifications. one revived her from ash.) while being assailed, alexis reflects on which tool of hers to employ. this is the singular important choice. ■ the last seven minutes of an episode bear the hallmarks of heaven. here alexis has made her decision, and that decision is the correct one. no ill befalls any thing or character past this point. villains do not receive comeuppance or humiliation, or they benefit from such. prisoners seem unbothered by captivity. pain is stripped of urgency as if by paint thinner. ■ for the entire first season i interpreted her as a take on me — i mean, honestly. omega slut, lady-courtesan. i may be a narcissist, but does it seem a reach? but in s2:e7, the tool she chooses is her voice, wreathed in a dress of shimmering emerald wings, and that must be me specifically. so it would be — incredibly weird and inelegant if the whole were also me. there are a few obvious other lenses to try. alexis is the gentle future. the children’s children’s children, after millennia and millennia of growth. perfect morality ascendant over creation. existing to us only in everdistance. alexis is witches in general. when she selects a tool, she is embodying and fashioning herself after one of them. each episode is plea or commentary from the creator to one of the forces of the world. alexis is dolls in general. there’s just so much emphasis on how she’s a creation. alexis is the marriage of dolls and witches. this is probably too abstract and i’m not sure it fundamentally works, but i think i’d need another watch to rule it out. alexis is seraphic. she endures evil then defeats it, both infallibly. alexis is the void. she ends problems. ■ as for what it’s trying to say with its formula — well, what varies? the problems differ massively in shape and scale; if they are esoterically united then how so eludes me. but dense thread runs through the tools she chooses. to name a few: kiss, blowjob, card game, headphones, dragon. (each is generosity, each is handcraft.) ■ at the start of the title is omega, then slut, then alexis as moefication of ‘aleph.’ so what we have is a continuous loop of… mess? defilement? purity? given the sparsity of dialogue, 'slut’ in the title contends powerfully for the most important word in the series. what then does it mean? someone who pleases as many others as possible? was the creator unable to find a word for a divine beast as intimately bound to serve mud as clouds as horses? the name stands out doubly because the show is rendered in a style typical to western children’s animation and it — never addresses this. its head is utterly elsewhere from the likes of south park or ddlc. it doesn’t see itself as a setup for betrayal. as emotions, the show is wholly bereft of horror or shock. alexis does not scold the world for its absurdity when her bathwater becomes rainbow tree frogs. she is confused and curious, but not for a moment does she lose faith in base logic. this is also the climax of the episode: she must upon the instant enact a complex miracle to avoid crushing or scaring any one of them. this commands several minutes of animation to depict. ■ terrible things oft happen to her clothes, because they’re trying to happen to her. and she chooses a form of sex as her tool several times, but when it happens on-screen it’s — slow. there’s something determined about it. sex is the closest omega slut alexis comes to violence. even the healthiest sex features values dissonance. participants might want something extremely similar to happen, but not the exact same thing. this is serious to alexis. the size of a problem has zero salience, only its existence. she carries sole responsibility for perfection. ■ as sublunary fiction — 8/10. the overarching plot beyond the formula is hazy and the animation shoestring, but i readily award points to any craft that pushes limits in novel ways. as an esoteric work — mm. i do not believe i grasp its soul. it attempts a rapid mélange of statements, only one of which is 'addressed’ to me. i need to let my thoughts percolate for a while.

i’ll try to be a light burden. you must have many tasks. perhaps i could help with your work. the tip of her slender finger touches my lips, cold and poreless. she brushes my left eye shut, then the right. she lifts and holds me like a teddy bear, legs dangling by her sides, though she is not much taller. i count her steps. there are hundreds. it’s exciting to reach one thousand — then two thousand. i recognize hardwood, a ladder, and for a while rooftop. then i can’t hear her steps, and it feels awful to lose track. we keep going. i don’t open my eyes. she lifts me up higher onto silken sheets, actuators trembling with a strained whir beneath the weight. there is no exhale of exertion; then her hands move away. i lie in bed enmeshed within an overlay of ticking. clear crystals and plastic trinkets and rainbow marbles catch the light above, wreathed and suspended in string. from a far corner or another room glides over me the faintness of windchimes. …put me back. she will miss me. be it in weeks or months, for love or nostalgia, she will look. i will not abide the violation of my loss. she nestles her face over my shoulder and very slightly, shakes her head.

beast-queen’s shape-changing organ, unweaving the fabric of it, so as to prevent its use. the second blow the challenger made to the beast-queen’s mouth, sintering lower jaw to upper, and preventing her from choosing the challenger as food. the third blow was simple and straightforward and spilled out the beast-queen’s life, marking the end of centuries on the hall floor. the beast-queen, being
